_meta.indication: Edarbi is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) indicated for the treatment of hypertension; it may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 01-05-TL-491-008, a Phase 3 double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study in essential hypertension
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo- and active (olmesartan)-controlled, 6-week study
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 6 in 24-hour mean systolic blood pressure (SBP) by ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)
pivotal_trials.n: A total of 1275 subjects were randomized
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-corrected change in 24-hour mean SBP: Edarbi 40 mg -12.08 mm Hg (95% CI -14.48, -9.67), 80 mg -13.21 mm Hg (95% CI -15.62, -10.81), both P<0.001 vs placebo

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Azilsartan Medoxomil in Participants With Essential Hypertension

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 01-06-TL-491-019, a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled 5-arm titration study vs valsartan and olmesartan
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled forced titration study comparing TAK-491 with placebo, olmesartan and valsartan after 6 weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 6 in 24-hour mean systolic blood pressure (SBP) by ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)
pivotal_trials.n: A total of 1291 subjects were randomized
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-corrected change in 24-hour mean SBP: Edarbi 40 mg -13.16 mm Hg (95% CI -15.41, -10.91), 80 mg -14.27 mm Hg (95% CI -16.54, -12.01), both P<0.001; Edarbi 80 mg superior to valsartan 320 mg (difference -4.31, 95% CI -6.25, -2.37, P<0.001) and to olmesartan 40 mg (difference -2.54, 95% CI -4.44, -0.64, P=0.009)

nct_ctgov.title: An Efficacy and Safety Study of Azilsartan Medoxomil Compared to Valsartan and Olmesartan in Participants With Essential Hypertension.

key_safety: Treatment was well-tolerated with an overall incidence of adverse reactions similar to placebo; the most common adverse reaction in adults was diarrhea (2% with Edarbi 80 mg vs 0.5% placebo). Withdrawals due to adverse events were 2.4% (placebo), 2.2% (40 mg) and 2.7% (80 mg). Increases in serum creatinine were more common with Edarbi than placebo, most apparent when co-administered with chlorthalidone
target_moa: Azilsartan medoxomil is a prodrug hydrolyzed to azilsartan, a selective AT1 subtype angiotensin II receptor antagonist that blocks the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II, the principal pressor agent of the renin-angiotensin system

boxed_warning.content: Fetal/neonatal morbidity and mortality: drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus; when pregnancy is detected, discontinue Edarbi as soon as possible

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication

basis.text: Priority Designation S (Standard review), not priority

summary.text: Edarbi (azilsartan medoxomil) was submitted under NDA 200796, filed 4/28/2010 as a standard (Priority Designation S) review, and approved for the treatment of hypertension based on blinded, placebo-controlled studies demonstrating blood-pressure lowering; it was not referred to an advisory committee and was not an accelerated approval

citations.quote: NDA #200796 was filed on 4/28/2010 as an electronic submission.

The primary medical and statistical reviewers recommended approval of azilsartan medoxomil for the treatment of hypertension. The reviewers concluded that the drug's ability to lower blood pressure was adequately shown in blinded, placebo-controlled studies.
